title: Boys and girls in London's registers
hook: 82 years of London christenings, counted by sex. How often were boys ahead?

knows: about as many boys as girls are born
doesNotKnow: that a small surplus of boys showed in every one of 82 years of London's christenings, because the counts were large

misconception: In old records, boys and girls come out about even, so any year could go either way.
objective: The learner can say that London christened more boys than girls in every one of 82 years (about 107 to 100), and that a small steady difference shows every year when the counts are large.

claims.text: London christened 484,382 boys and 453,841 girls from 1629 to 1710 (82 years), with counts for each year.
claims.source: history-data.mjs: arbuthnot, Arbuthnot.csv, columns Males and Females (Arbuthnot 1710, per the HistData doc). Copied into Demo.tsx as CHRISTENED. Known trap (charter): the 1674 and 1704 rows are identical in the file; both are drawn as given.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Re-derived in my own node script from the pinned file (history-data.mjs pins all hold; sha256 re-checked) and compared with the copied array in Demo.tsx (identical). Arbuthnot.csv Males sum 484,382, Females 453,841, 82 rows 1629-1710; Demo.tsx CHRISTENED identical. The 1674 and 1704 rows are identical (6,113 / 5,738); the HistData doc (Zabell) says the 1704 values were 'probably copied erroneously from the former'.

claims.text: Boys outnumbered girls at christening in all 82 years, by about 107 to 100 overall; the closest year, 1703, had 101 boys for every 100 girls and the widest, 1661, had 116.
claims.source: history-cycle2-check.mjs section 16: 82 of 82; 100 x 484,382 / 453,841 = 106.7 -> 107; min ratio 1703 (101.1 -> 101), max 1661 (115.6 -> 116). Demo.tsx computes the same from CHRISTENED; stage and reveal both use Math.round.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): 82 of 82 years Males > Females; 106.73 (107); min 1703 101.07 (101); max 1661 115.61 (116). Note, not blocking: one of the 82 years (1704) is probably a copying error, so the record has 81 independent years. Arbuthnot's own argument used all 82, and the lesson draws them as given.

claims.text: London christened 5,612 to 16,145 babies a year, so the small surplus showed every year (reveal; axis title 'boys minus girls, of 5,612–16,145 a year').
claims.source: history-data.mjs: arbuthnot, Arbuthnot.csv, Males + Females per year (CHRISTENED, re-derived in node from the pinned file 2026-10-15, sha256 d81babe6... matches): smallest 1650, 2,890 + 2,722 = 5,612; largest 1705, 8,366 + 7,779 = 16,145; mean 11,442. 'So the small surplus showed every year': with these counts the yearly surplus is 82 to 800 (stage), above zero in all 82 years (c2); the simulation (c5) shows the same split at 100 a year does not. The general point (sampling noise falls with count) is owned by probability; stated here as what the record and the simulation show.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): Each year's counts are 2,722-8,426 per sex; yearly surplus 82-800, all above zero. As stated. | v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-15, W-990, learner r1 finding 1): was 'A small, steady difference shows every single year once the counts are in the thousands.' (told, not shown). Now the yearly totals are on the stage and a labelled simulation stands for the cause. Reset to unverified for a fact-checker who is not the builder. | FC pass 47 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Rendered: axis title 'boys minus girls, of 5,612–16,145 a year'; reveal 'London christened 5,612 to 16,145 babies a year, so the small surplus showed every year.' Own node script on the pinned Arbuthnot.csv (sha256 d81babe6... matches); Demo.tsx CHRISTENED = the file's 82 rows, 0 mismatches. Males + Females: smallest 1650, 2,890 + 2,722 = 5,612; largest 1705, 8,366 + 7,779 = 16,145. Yearly surplus 82 to 800, above zero in 82 of 82 years. 'So ... showed every year': with p = 0.51628, even the smallest year's expected surplus is 2.4 standard deviations above zero (normal approximation, n = 5,612), against an expected 27.5 of 82 years with girls ahead at 100 a year (exact binomial P(girls ahead) = 0.335); the simulation (c5) shows this on stage.

claims.text: Simulated with only 100 christenings a year and the same split, girls led in 23 of 82 years (reveal; 'If only 100 a year (simulated)' view: headline 'simulation: girls ahead in 23 of 82 years', and, back on the real chart, the line 'simulated, 100 a year: girls ahead 23 of 82' below zero). This is a simulation, not data.
claims.source: Demo.tsx SIM: 82 years x 100 draws, each a boy if rng() < p, p = 484,382 / (484,382 + 453,841) = 0.51628 (the file's overall share), rng = mulberry32(1) from src/kit/random.ts, drawn in year order. Seed 1: boys ahead 55, tied 4, girls ahead 23; yearly boys minus girls from -22 to +24. Seed 1 is the first seed tried and was not chosen for its result (pattern disclose-chosen-seeds). Spread over seeds 1-1000 (node, 2026-10-15): girls ahead median 27.5 (the 500th and 501st sorted values are 27 and 28), 5th-95th percentile 20 to 35, range 14 to 41; so every seed tried shows girls ahead in at least 14 years, and seed 1's 23 is on the low side of typical. The chart's scale in this view is one tenth of the real one (ticks +40, +80, −40).
claims.note: v2 (demo-builder, 2026-10-15, W-990): new, the learner r1 'if only 100 a year' control. Not verified by the builder. | FC pass 47 (fact-checker, 2026-10-15): VERIFIED. Rendered: headline 'simulation: girls ahead in 23 of 82 years', readout 'SIMULATED, 100 A YEAR girls ahead 23 of 82', ticks '−40, 0, +40, +80', back on the real chart 'simulated, 100 a year: girls ahead 23 of 82'; reveal 'Simulated with only 100 a year and the same split, girls led in 23 of 82 years.' Own re-implementation of mulberry32 from src/kit/random.ts (typed from the source, not imported), p = 484,382 / 938,223 = 0.516276, 82 years x 100 draws in year order, boy if rng() < p: seed 1 gives girls ahead 23, tied 4, boys ahead 55, yearly boys minus girls -22 to +24 (fits the ±40 scale). Seeds 1-1000: girls ahead min 14, max 41, 5th percentile 20, 95th 35, median 27.5 (the 500th and 501st sorted values are 27 and 28); 18.3% of seeds give 23 or fewer. Exact expectation 82 x 0.335 = 27.5. The stage and reveal say 'simulated' and quote seed 1's count only, so the sentence holds. Advisory, not blocking: the source field and the Demo.tsx header say 'median 28'; with 1,000 seeds it is 27.5. Seed 1 sits below typical (as the source field already says); whether it was the first seed tried cannot be checked from the artifact. | v3 (demo-builder, 2026-10-15, FC47 advisory): source 'median 28' corrected to 27.5 (re-run in node over seeds 1-1000: median 27.5, 5th-95th 20 to 35, range 14 to 41, seed 1 = 23). Text unchanged. Reset to unverified for a fact-checker who is not the builder.

claims.text: Where it stops: these are christenings in London, not births, so babies who were never christened are missing.
claims.source: history-data.mjs: arbuthnot, HistData Arbuthnot documentation (christenings by sex in London). Brief #16: no held source sentence.
claims.note: FC pass 39 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): HistData Arbuthnot doc (opened), quoting Oeppen: 'Arbuthnot's data are annual counts of public baptisms, not births. Birth-baptism delay meant that infant deaths could occur before baptism.'

recall.question: Boys are 51% of births. Which hospital more often has a day with more girls than boys: one with 10 births a day or one with 1,000?
recall.why: With few births a day, chance swamps a small surplus; with 1,000 the 51% shows almost every day, as London's thousands of christenings did every year.
